Lab 01 — step by step, animated

Integrative Project, Part 1: map a small network and write its monitoring plan (5 %) — 420-1C1-DW Preventative Monitoring, LEA.D8, Dawson College. This page shows each step of the Lab 1 guide as a short schematic animation: what you click, what you type, what the result must look like. The animations are drawings, not screenshots — the real applications change their look from one version to the next; the version note under each animation says what may differ.

Step 0

Before you start — the rules that apply to every lab

≈ 5 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. Sign Annex A of the Legal Notice before any laboratory access (the e-signature page is provided separately; using the materials binds you to the Notice anyway — section 2.2).
  2. Work only on the fictional workshop, Ébénisterie Val-des-Pins Inc. (Legal Notice 6.4 "Keep it fictional", 6.7, 18.2).
  3. Check every link and every download: read the domain, scan the URL on VirusTotal, verify the SHA-256 checksum (Annex C).

Do not

  • Touch any real network — the College's, your home Wi-Fi, an employer's — "just to look" (6.1, 6.3).
  • Capture, scan or install an agent anywhere; Lab 1 needs no network activity at all (7.2, 7.6).
  • Put real names, addresses, credentials or screenshots in a submission (6.7, 18.2).

Why

Some of what the course teaches is indistinguishable from an attack when performed without permission. Authorization is everything: if you are not certain that you have it, you do not have it (6.1.3).

Step 1

Install the free tools from their official sites

≈ 20 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. diagrams.net (draw.io) desktop from the official GitHub releases page, or the browser version at diagrams.net — for the network map.
  2. LibreOffice 26.8 (August 2026) or the 26.2 / 25.8 branches — Writer for the plan, Calc for the registers.
  3. Python 3.12 or newer (3.14 is the current line) — only if you want to run class7_prioritize.py; tick "Add python.exe to PATH" on Windows.
  4. Verify each download: Windows certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256 · macOS shasum -a 256 <file> · Linux sha256sum <file>.

Do not

  • Download from mirrors, "download managers" or search-engine advertisements (Annex C).
  • Use cracked, patched or unlicensed software; every open-source tool has a licence you must respect (6.6).

Why

A tampered installer is the easiest way to lose your own computer. Official source + checksum = the two checks every professional makes.

Version note (September 2026): Versions move: LibreOffice publishes a new branch every February and August, Python every October (3.15 is scheduled for October 2026), and the diagrams.net desktop app is released several times a year. The installer screens you see may differ slightly from this schematic; the five checks do not change.
Links: diagrams.net · diagrams.net desktop — official releases · LibreOffice download · Python downloads
Step 2

Get the lab base from Léa into one folder

≈ 5 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. Create the folder Lab01_<StudentNumber> and download into it the Class 7 companion files: class7_table0…6_*.csv, class7_prioritize.py, the figures — and your own Class 6 registers (inventory, constraints, monitoring needs).
  2. Keep the originals unchanged; work on copies. The tables are worked examples and templates, not the answer key.

Do not

  • Share the course files, sample solutions or this guide with anyone, including other cohorts (4.3, 17.2).

Why

The registers and the plan of Lab 1 are the foundation of Labs 2 and 3; the base files give every student the same starting network so that the reasoning — not the data entry — is what is graded.

Step 3

Draw the network map (Deliverable 1)

≈ 45 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. File → New → Blank diagram; open More shapes… → Networking.
  2. Internet cloud on top, MAIL-CLOUD beside it, outside the perimeter; FW-01 below; SW-01 for the server room and office (SRV-FILE-01, NAS-01, PC-ACCT-01, PRN-01, PC-OFFICE-01…05, AP-01); SW-02 for the shop floor (CNC-PC-01, PC-SHOP-01).
  3. Show the guest Wi-Fi greyed and marked "excluded (owner, Class 6)"; label every link (wired / Wi-Fi / provider); add your variation.
  4. File → Export as → PNG at 200 %; keep the .drawio source; use only the fictional addressing of Class 6.

Do not

  • Use a real network, real addresses or a vendor's logos copied from the web.
  • Forget the naming key: every asset carries exactly the identifier of Table 0.

Why

Section 1 of the plan; Lab 2 installs the monitoring tool on this map, and Lab 3 reports an anomaly against it.

Version note (September 2026): diagrams.net renames menu entries occasionally ("Export as" has also appeared as "Export"); the Networking shape library is present in every 2025–2026 release. Any drawing tool from the alternatives list is acceptable if the result is a PNG plus its editable source.
Links: diagrams.net · Table 0 — naming key (lecture page, Downloads)
Step 4

Fill the registers — criticality, exposure, score, tier (sections 4 and 5)

≈ 60 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. Open copies of class7_table2 and class7_table3 in Calc; save as Lab01_<StudentNumber>_register.ods (or .xlsx).
  2. Per asset: C, I, A from 1 to 3 → criticality = the highest (high-water mark, NIST FIPS 199); E1–E5 as 0 or 1 → sum → Low 1 (0–1), Moderate 2 (2–3), High 3 (4–5); score = criticality × exposure; tier 6–9 = 1, 3–4 = 2, 1–2 = 3.
  3. One sentence of your own per asset; PC-OFFICE-01…05 rated as a group and said so; GUEST-WIFI recorded as an exclusion (reason, decided by, date); a review date on every row; rate your variation.
  4. Copy the envelope of Table 1 into section 5 (2,275 MB/day, 60 min/day, dated, agreed with the owner).

Do not

  • Add the three impact ratings or average them — the rule is the highest.
  • Name a person in the exposure facts; write about the asset (6.7, 7.2).

Why

The register is where criticality (how bad) and exposure (how likely) meet; every later decision is defended from these two columns.

Version note (September 2026): LibreOffice Calc 26.x opens a .csv with the dialog "Text Import" (separator: comma, character set: UTF-8); Excel and Google Sheets show an equivalent dialog. Formulas are optional — the calculator script does the same arithmetic.
Links: NIST FIPS 199 · NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 · CVE · NVD
Step 5

Compute the order of work and fit it into the envelope (sections 6 and 7)

≈ 30 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. Either edit the CRITICALITY, EXPOSURE and ACTIVITY blocks of class7_prioritize.py and run python3 class7_prioritize.py (Windows: py class7_prioritize.py), or do the same steps in Calc.
  2. Sort by score, then higher criticality, then higher exposure, then lower MB/day; add activities while both totals stay within 2,275 MB and 60 min per day.
  3. A Tier 1 activity that does not fit: try the reduced activity first (connection records instead of a full capture); defer the rest with the reason and the review date (Oct 16, 2026); justify any override (a dependency or a legal obligation is accepted; anything else needs the owner's sign-off).
  4. Paste the table into section 6 and the deferred list into section 7.

Do not

  • Drop a Tier 1 asset silently — a gap that is not written down is a surprise, not a decision.
  • Let cost override the two ratings: it is the last tie-breaker, not the first.

Why

Section 6 is the order in which Lab 2 installs the monitoring tool; section 7 is where Lab 3 starts its optimizations.

Version note (September 2026): The script needs only the Python standard library; if python3 is not found on Windows, use py, or open the file in the IDLE editor installed with Python and press F5. The output shown is the worked example — yours changes with your ratings and your variation.
Links: Python downloads · CCCS — baseline controls for small and medium organizations
Step 6

Write the monitoring plan (Deliverable 2)

≈ 60 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. In Writer, the nine headings in this order: 1 scope and network map · 2 constraints · 3 monitoring needs · 4 asset register · 5 resource envelope · 6 ordered activities · 7 exclusions and deferred activities · 8 review cycle · 9 legal and privacy statement.
  2. Keep 1–3 short (your Class 6 work); paste the registers and the order as tables; expand every abbreviation on first use.
  3. Section 9: all data is fictional; no real personal information, credentials or organization data (18.2); how future captures and logs will be stored, minimized and deleted (6.7, 7.2).
  4. File → Export As → Export as PDF → Lab01_<StudentNumber>_plan.pdf.

Do not

  • Turn the plan into a list of tools — it is the written reasoning that turns an inventory into an ordered set of activities.

Why

A decision that is not written down cannot be reviewed, defended or improved; the plan is the deliverable that an auditor, the owner or next year's technician reads.

Version note (September 2026): Writer's PDF export dialog gained new tabs in the 25.x and 26.x branches; the default settings are correct. Word, ONLYOFFICE, Google Docs or Markdown converted with Pandoc are acceptable as long as the submission is a PDF.
Links: LibreOffice · Pandoc · ISEP — Institutional Student Evaluation Policy
Step 7

Check and submit — Léa DropBox, Sunday, October 11, 2026, 23:59 EDT

≈ 15 min
Schematic animation, not a screenshot of the real software — the layout of the actual application may differ.

What you do

  1. Run the checklist: map complete; registers with the highest-of-three rule and correct sums; totals within the envelope; reduction before deferral; sections 7, 8, 9 present; no real data anywhere.
  2. Files named Lab01_<StudentNumber>_map.png, the .drawio source, Lab01_<StudentNumber>_plan.pdf and the register file; upload all of them to the Lab 1 DropBox in Léa.
  3. One submission per student; a resubmission before the deadline replaces the previous one.

Do not

  • Wait for the last hour: the late policy is 10 % per day and nothing is accepted after 7 days.
  • Send the files by e-mail or MIO instead of the DropBox.

Why

The DropBox time stamp is the submission time; midnight EDT on October 11 is 23:59, not 00:00 of October 12.

Version note (September 2026): Léa's DropBox screen is maintained by the College; button labels may differ from this schematic. Questions during the session go through the class chat, afterwards by MIO (Messagerie interne Omnivox).
